text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Consumer Price Index up 0.4 per cent -- lowest September increase since 1968.
- Government considers joint hot pursuit units in Hebron.
- Jordan's King Hussein returns to Jericho.
- Intelligence head: Syria preparing war option.
- U.S. to maintain military aid, Defence Secretary William Perry tells Israeli counterpart Yitzhak Mordechai.
- Former Soviet Jewish dissident and Israeli Trade Minister Natan Sharansky defeats world chess champion Garry Kasparov.
- Bank of Israel: Economic slowdown continued in third quarter.
- Managing Director of the Mifal Hapayis lottery Shmuel Slavin will replace Treasury director-general David Brodett early next year.
- First International Bank offers provident fund with guaranteed real yield.
- Cairo summit organisers expect 1,000 businesses to attend.
- Movenpick opens here, will invest 150 million shekels in 10 motels.
- Jerusalem reasearchers develop chip to aid surgeons.
GLOBES
- Finance Minister Dan Meridor calls for immediate drop in interest rates of 1.0 percentage point following September CPI rise of only 0.4 percent.
- Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel: The slowdown -- an important element in a decision on the interest rate.
HAARETZ
- Jordan's King Hussein secretly met an Israeli envoy in London last weekend, and since then he has moderated his attacks on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
- Head of strategic research centre in Israel says chances of military putsch in Israel are growing.
- Intelligence services in West believe Islamist government in Turkey will fall soon.
- Deputy Military Intelligence Chief Amos Gilad: "The Syrians are training for a military option and will act in accordance with developments".
- Expectation Frenkel will lower interest rates by 0.5 percentage point.
MAARIV
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat: The negotiations are stuck. Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy: The agreement -- within days.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu worried about economic slowdown. Assessment: Frenkel will lower the interest rate.
- Ten years ago today airman Ron Arad fell into captivity.
- Arafat proposes stationing American troops in Hebron.
- Reports from Paris: French President Jacques Chirac will be first head of state to speak to Palestinian council.
